incident.name: Checkmarx + Bitwarden CI/CD Supply Chain
incident.vector: Trojanized security scanner + password manager CLI
incident.description: Attackers trojanized Checkmarx KICS (IaC security scanner) and Bitwarden CLI npm package simultaneously, targeting CI/CD pipelines across 50,000+ businesses. Stolen GitHub tokens used to inject malicious Actions workflows downstream. Followed earlier compromise of Aqua Security's Trivy scanner.
incident.root_cause: Over-privileged CI/CD pipeline dependencies, no behavioral monitoring of security tools
incident.lessons: Security tools embedded in CI/CD pipelines are the highest-value supply chain targets. Pipeline dependencies must be treated as first-class attack surface.

relatedIncidents.name: Yahoo Data Breach
relatedIncidents.description: All 3 billion Yahoo accounts compromised. Largest data breach in history. Disclosed 2 years after breach.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: Weak MD5 hashing, no breach detection, delayed disclosure
relatedIncidents.lessons: Strong password hashing (bcrypt/Argon2) and breach detection are essential.

relatedIncidents.name: Uber Data Breach
relatedIncidents.description: Teen hacker used MFA fatigue attack on contractor, then pivoted via Slack to access AWS, GCP, and internal systems.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: MFA fatigue, over-privileged contractor access, poor secrets management
relatedIncidents.lessons: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) and least-privilege access are essential.

relatedIncidents.name: LastPass Breach
relatedIncidents.description: Attacker compromised developer laptop, stole source code, then used it to breach cloud storage containing encrypted password vaults.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: Compromised developer endpoint, insufficient secrets separation
relatedIncidents.lessons: Developer workstations are high-value targets. Secrets must be isolated from source code.
